title: Checkpoint: World 4
objectives: Apply everything learned in World 4 (FOR, WHILE, DO-WHILE, counters/accumulators, infinite loops, nested loops, trace tables) together

hook.text: You have reached the end of World 4. Now it is time to test your loop skills with mixed questions.

concept.heading: Checkpoint
concept.body: This lesson does not teach a new topic; it reinforces what you have learned. The questions below test all the loop types and their common mistakes in a mix.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
Which loop is preferred if the number of rounds is not known in advance?

feedback.correct: Correct. When the number of rounds is unknown, a WHILE (condition-based) loop is used.
feedback.incorrect: WHILE is better suited to an unknown number of rounds.

exercises.question: What is the difference between DO-WHILE and WHILE?
options: DO-WHILE checks the condition at the end, so the body runs at least once
There is no difference between them

feedback.correct: Correct. DO-WHILE is a post-test loop, so the body is guaranteed to run at least once.
feedback.incorrect: The difference is the place of the check: DO-WHILE checks at the end, so the body runs at least once.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: The multiples of 3 from 1 to 6 are 3 and 6.

exercises.question: What is the most common reason a WHILE loop runs forever?
options: Forgetting to update, inside the loop, the variable that affects the condition

feedback.correct: Correct. If the update is forgotten, the condition never becomes FALSE.
feedback.incorrect: The most common reason is that the variable that affects the condition is not updated inside the loop.

exercises.question: If the outer loop runs 4 times and the inner loop runs 2 times in each round, how many times does the inner body run in total?

feedback.incorrect: The total number of repetitions is outer times inner: 4 × 2 = 8.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: The statement "total ← total + x" is an update of an ___.

exercises.question: Write an algorithm that adds up the even numbers from 1 to 10.
exercises.sampleSolution:
total ← 0
FOR i ← 1 TO 10 STEP 1
  IF i MOD 2 = 0
    total ← total + i
  END
END_LOOP
WRITE total

summary: World 4 complete: FOR, WHILE, DO-WHILE, counters/accumulators, infinite loops, nested loops, trace tables.
These skills will be used directly in World 5 when you work with arrays.
You will see the topics you struggled with again in your review queue.
